description: Three transcriptional repressors (LacI, TetR, CI) form a cyclic negative-feedback loop: LacI represses tetR, TetR represses cI, and CI represses lacI. Each of the three genes is represented by its mRNA concentration m_i and its protein concentration p_i, giving 6 coupled ODEs. Transcription of gene i is repressed by the protein of the preceding gene j; repression is described by a Hill function of coefficient n, and a leaky (fully repressed) transcription term a0 is included. mRNA is degraded with rate 1 (time is rescaled in units of the mRNA lifetime), protein is degraded with the ratio beta of protein-to-mRNA decay rates, and translation is captured by the beta*m_i term. This is the model used in the paper to predict that the network can either converge to a stable steady state or produce sustained limit-cycle oscillations.
missing_information: The dimensionless parameters alpha, alpha0 and beta are not printed numerically in the paper; they must be derived from the raw kinetic values, and the conversion is convention-dependent (alpha lies between 30 and 216 depending on whether the quoted half-lives are used as lifetimes or as exponential decay constants).

Initial conditions for the simulations in Fig. 1c are not given in the paper. The values stored in this IR (m_i = 0; p_lacI = 3, p_tetR = 1, p_cI = 0) are ASSUMED by us solely to allow numerical integration, and are deliberately asymmetric so that the symmetric steady state is not approached trivially.
The exact parameter set marked by 'X' in the stability diagram (Fig. 1b) is not tabulated, and the axis ranges of Fig. 1b cannot be read reliably from the OCR text.
The duration of the numerical integration and the sampling/output times used in Fig. 1c are not specified.
No absolute fluorescence calibration or error bars are given for the measured period (160 +/- 40 min), so model-to-data comparison can only be qualitative.
model_name: Repressilator: symmetric cyclic negative-feedback oscillator (Elowitz & Leibler, Box 1, continuous deterministic model)

assumptions: The three repressors are treated as identical except for their DNA-binding specificity (symmetric repressilator), as stated in Box 1.
Repression of transcription is described by the Hill function a/(1+p^n) plus a constant leak term a0.
Transcription, translation and degradation are treated as continuous and deterministic; the discrete/stochastic nature of the molecules is neglected (this is the paper's continuous approximation).
Time is rescaled in units of the mRNA lifetime (1 time unit = 2 min); protein concentrations are written in units of K_M; mRNA concentrations are rescaled by their translation efficiency.

The dimensionless parameter alpha was not printed numerically in the paper; it was derived from the printed kinetic values (0.5 transcripts/s max, 5e-4 transcripts/s leaky, 20 proteins/transcript, protein half-life 10 min, mRNA half-life 2 min, K_M = 40 per cell), treating the quoted half-lives as exponential decay constants (alpha ~ 216, alpha0 ~ 0.216, beta = 0.2).

ASSUMED initial conditions: the paper does not state the initial conditions used in Fig. 1c. We used m_i = 0 for all three mRNAs and p_lacI = 3, p_tetR = 1, p_cI = 0. These are arbitrary but asymmetric; the resulting attractor (limit cycle vs. steady state) does not depend on this choice as long as the symmetric initial condition is avoided.
origin.source_text: M. B. Elowitz & S. Leibler, 'A synthetic oscillatory network of transcriptional regulators', Nature 403, 335-338 (2000), Box 1 (continuous deterministic approximation) and Fig. 1b,c

parameters.description: Maximum (fully induced) promoter strength in rescaled units, equal to the maximum number of protein copies per cell divided by K_M. Derived from the paper's explicit kinetic values: 0.5 transcripts s^-1 (fully induced) x 20 proteins per transcript x protein half-life 10 min, divided by K_M = 40 monomers per cell, using exponential decay rates (gamma_p = ln2/10 min, gamma_m = ln2/2 min), giving alpha ~ 216.
parameters.name: alpha
parameters.unit: dimensionless (max proteins per cell, in units of K_M)

parameters.description: Leakiness of the promoter: transcription rate with saturating repressor. The paper gives 5e-4 transcripts s^-1 repressed vs 0.5 transcripts s^-1 fully induced, i.e. alpha0/alpha = 1e-3 (the same ratio used for curve C in Fig. 1b).
parameters.name: alpha0

parameters.description: Ratio of protein decay rate to mRNA decay rate. From the paper's stated half-lives (protein 10 min, mRNA 2 min): beta = 2/10 = 0.2, equal to the ratio of protein lifetime to mRNA lifetime.
parameters.name: beta
parameters.unit: dimensionless (ratio of protein to mRNA decay rate)

parameters.description: Hill coefficient (cooperativity) of transcriptional repression; the paper states n = 2 for the numerical solution in Fig. 1c.
parameters.name: n

variables.description: lacI mRNA concentration, rescaled by its translation efficiency (proteins produced per mRNA)
variables.name: m_lacI
p_lacI

variables.name: m_tetR
